facts.statement: Loricatosaurus is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur meaning "armored lizard".
facts.quote: Loricatosaurus (meaning "armored lizard") is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur known from Callovian-aged (Middle Jurassic) rocks of England and France.

facts.statement: The type species was first discovered in November 1901 by Alfred Leeds at the Fletton brick pit in England.
facts.quote: Loricatosaurus is known from remains previously assigned to Lexovisaurus that were first discovered at the Fletton brick pit in the Oxford Clay Formation, Fletton, Peterborough, England, by Alfred Leeds during November 1901.

facts.statement: The remains were originally named Stegosaurus priscus by Baron Franz Nopcsa in 1911.
facts.quote: The material was later named Stegosaurus priscus ("ancient roofed lizard") by Baron Franz Nopcsa in 1911 and Lexovisaurus by Hoffstetter, 1957 and Peter Galton, 1985.

facts.statement: In 2008, Susannah Maidment and colleagues reclassified the species into a new genus named Loricatosaurus.
facts.quote: However, upon later review of the material in 2008, Susannah Maidment and colleagues determined that Lexovisaurus was based upon nondiagnostic remains, and coined a new genus for Lexovisaurus priscus and its referred specimen.

facts.statement: The genus is known from only two partial skeletons.
facts.quote: It is known from only two partial skeletons.

facts.statement: Unlike previous reports, no shoulder spine is present in the known material, and any spine-like structure is likely from the tail.
facts.quote: Contrary to previous reports (as Lexovisaurus), a shoulder spine is not present in the known material; the possible spine is more likely from the tail.

facts.statement: Loricatosaurus lived during the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic in England and France.
facts.quote: Loricatosaurus (meaning "armored lizard") is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur known from Callovian-aged (Middle Jurassic) rocks of England and France.

facts.statement: Loricatosaurus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Loricatosaurus belongs to the parent group Stegosaurinae.
Loricatosaurus is classified in the family Stegosauridae.
Loricatosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including vertebrae, limb bones, and armor plates.
facts.quote: The holotype (NHMUK R3167) is a partial skeleton, including two cervical, six dorsal, and 16 caudal vertebrae, a right humerus and right ulna, some carpus, two metacarpals (one incomplete), a partial ilia, partial right ischium, and pubis, the left femur, partial tibia and fibula, fused tarsals, and some armour plates.

facts.statement: The initial discovery included a semi-articulated skeleton with vertebrae, partial limbs, pelvis, and fragmentary dermal armor.
facts.quote: Leeds collected a semi articulated skeleton consisting of two cervical, six dorsal, and 16 caudal vertebrae, a partial right forelimb, partial left hindlimb, partial pelves, and some fragmentary dermal armor.

facts.statement: A piece of armor previously described as a parascapular spine is actually a fragmentary tail spine.
facts.quote: One piece of armor was described as a parascapular spine, but it is actually a fragmentary tail spine.

facts.statement: A second specimen was briefly referred to Lexovisaurus in 1957 before being properly described in 1985.
facts.quote: In 1957, another specimen now referred to Loricatosaurus was briefly referred to Lexovisaurus until a more proper description was made in 1985 by Peter Galton.

facts.statement: A second specimen from Normandy, France, includes many vertebrae and a dorsal spine.
facts.quote: The specimen was a partial postcranial skeleton, including many vertebrae and a dorsal spine, from the Lower Callovian of Le Fresne d'Argences (Calvados), Normandy, France.

facts.statement: A 2025 analysis recovered Loricatosaurus as the sister taxon to an unnamed Chinese stegosaur within the Stegosaurinae.
facts.quote: A 2025 publication by Sánchez-Fenollosa & Cobos included Loricatosaurus in a phylogenetic analysis and recovered it as the sister taxon to an unnamed stegosaur from the Qigu Formation of China within the Stegosaurinae.

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Loricatosaurus as a basal genus within the family Stegosauridae.
rejected.quote: Multiple phylogenetic analyses carried out by S. Maidment and O. Mateus between 2008 and 2010 place Loricatosaurus as a basal genus within the family Stegosauridae.
